reasoning_traces.think:
The HEADSport Filter Method provides a spectral artifact suppression mechanism for iMG data, ensuring that subsequent neural models receive clean inputs. It operates under the assumption of stationary noise and linear system behavior, which holds across 72 lab impacts and 5,694 field events. The CNN Brain Strains model then maps these cleaned kinematics to brain strain estimates using a convolutional architecture trained on finite-element simulations. This establishes a direct causal link between sensor input and injury risk prediction. The Impact Retriever complements this by solving the inverse problem—inferring impact origin and magnitude from the same kinematic data, thereby enriching the telemetry with contextual information. Together, these primitives form a closed-loop inference system where each component refines the next, enabling robust GSI probabilistic modeling and GSE situational awareness.
